text:
maria: heads up — after the canary deploy we see ~12% host CPU bump on the ingress preprocess path, mainly in tokenization + proto unpack. noticed an uptick in small write/syscall counts too.
kevin: saw the alert. which samples do you have? flame graphs or perf records?
maria: uploaded two perf dumps to /tmp/ingress-perf-1719209999.tar.gz and a small pprof export. hotspots look like parse_proto, stream_chunker::emit, grpc::writev. KV cache eviction spikes at the same time.
jonas: can you paste the pprof top (even rough numbers) and request size distro?
maria: pprof top (rough):
```
CPU Flat 40% parse_proto
CPU Flat 25% stream_chunker::emit
CPU Flat 15% grpc::writev
CPU Flat 10% tokenizer::tokenize
```
maria: request sizes: median ~480 tokens, p95 ~3.2k. lots of very short requests (100-300 tokens) creating many tiny writev()s and small batches.
kevin: sounds like batching heuristic is tuned for longer sequences — many tiny requests cause many small batches + kernel selection picks wide-kernel optimized for long seqs (bad fit). also writev churn hurts kernel throughput.
jonas: KV cache thrash looks real — eviction rate up ~3x during the window. my hypothesis: parse produces many ephemeral prefixes (variable-length spans) so keys are high-cardinality.
maria: triage plan: revert the micro change to parse prelude (PR #842), add a short coalescing layer in the ingress proxy, and change batching hint to prefer time-based flush for short seqs.
kevin: SGTM. quick experiment: in proxy set `coalesce_bytes=4096` and `time_flush_ms=8` and bench 1k rps of short requests. should reduce small writes.
jonas: also instrument kernel-selection logging so we emit chosen kernel + seq_len histo per model, that will let us see if long-kernel is being picked incorrectly.
maria: will run the bench now, attaching the bench command: `wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --script short_chat.lua http://ingress-canary.local/generate`
ci-bot: deploy started: rollup/ingress-prep-fixes at 1719210050
kevin: also worth normalizing KV keys before store: trim to first 64 bytes / canonicalize whitespace. reduces slot churn and keeps hot prefixes hot.
jonas: i'll add a `miss_by_prefix_len` metric in KV so we can validate the change.
maria: bench results (canary -> proxy with coalesce + time flush): latency p95 -18%, host CPU -9%, KV misses -40% (first pass). full traces and flame graphs uploaded to /artifacts/ingress/1719209999/.
kevin: excellent. let's push the canary to 20% and watch for any regression. add an alert for grpc writev syscall rate. :thumbsup: 
maria: rolling to 20% now and will keep an eye on kernel selection logs + KV metrics.
jonas: follow-up: add CI perf test that runs short-request microbench to catch tokenization/proto unpack regressions in future.
maria: thanks everyone — will post the dashboard after the 20% roll finishes.
